meta.policy: Curated and hand-verified against primary sources on the curation date (vendor pages, official Hugging Face repos and file listings, official GitHub repositories). It is NOT automatically current: model files, licenses and runtime support change. Use the live Hugging Face check on each model card to compare against today's metadata.
meta.sizeUnit: All file sizes are decimal GB (1 GB = 1,000,000,000 bytes) as listed by the repository. Users' VRAM/RAM figures are treated as GiB (2^30 bytes) by the recommendation engine because that is how GPUs and RAM kits are sold.

basis.file: Measured: exact file size from the repository file listing or the repository's own quant table.
basis.derived: Computed by the Atlas from official parameters or config.json (e.g. parameters x bytes, KV-cache from layer counts). Reproducible, but not a vendor statement.
basis.rough: Unverified rough estimate kept from the previous Atlas snapshot or extrapolated. Do not rely on it.

runtimes.name: llama.cpp
runtimes.summary: Portable C/C++ inference engine and the reference implementation for GGUF. Runs on CUDA, Metal, Vulkan, HIP and CPU and can split a model between GPU and system RAM.
runtimes.notes: MoE expert offload (--n-cpu-moe / --cpu-moe) and KV-cache quantisation (--cache-type-k / --cache-type-v) exist as options; check your build's --help.

runtimes.name: LM Studio
runtimes.license: Proprietary, free to use (see LM Studio terms)
runtimes.summary: Desktop app for discovering, downloading and serving local models through its own llama.cpp and MLX runtimes, with an OpenAI-compatible local server. Also hosts the Bionic agent environment.
runtimes.notes: Model support depends on the bundled runtime version; a new architecture may need a runtime update.

runtimes.name: Ollama
runtimes.summary: Local model runner with a simple CLI and REST API. Pulls models from its own library or imports GGUF files.
runtimes.notes: Architecture support depends on the Ollama version. Unless a model card lists Ollama, treat support as unverified.

runtimes.name: vLLM
runtimes.summary: High-throughput GPU serving engine built around batching and paged KV cache. Designed for models resident in GPU memory (single or multi-GPU); not a typical choice for RAM-offloaded single-user setups.
runtimes.notes: Atlas treats a model as vLLM-usable only if it fits in GPU memory.

runtimes.name: SGLang
runtimes.summary: GPU serving/runtime system for LLM and multimodal workloads with structured-generation features. Same memory model as vLLM: weights are expected to live in GPU memory.
runtimes.notes: Atlas treats a model as SGLang-usable only if it fits in GPU memory.

runtimes.name: MLX / MLX-LM
runtimes.summary: Apple's array framework for Apple silicon. Uses unified memory; MLX-format weights are separate downloads from GGUF.

runtimes.name: PrismML llama.cpp fork
runtimes.summary: Fork of llama.cpp that adds the PTQ1_0 / PQ2_0 low-bit formats used by Bonsai 2 GGUF files. Stock llama.cpp rejects these formats.
runtimes.notes: Do not mix the fork's ggml libraries with a stock llama.cpp build (fork README).

runtimes.name: Hugging Face Transformers
runtimes.summary: Reference Python library for research and prototyping. Flexible, but not tuned for lowest memory or highest throughput.

models.name: Gemma 4 E2B

kv.note: Approximation from config.json (35 layers, 20 KV-shared layers); tiny either way.

models.summary: Smallest Gemma 4 model. Text, image and audio input; aimed at phones, laptops and other constrained devices.
caveats: Google's own memory table lists ~2.9 GB for Q4_0, but the published QAT GGUF file is 3.35 GB, so use the file size.

models.name: Gemma 4 E4B

kv.note: Approximation from config.json (42 layers, 18 KV-shared layers).

models.summary: Compact multimodal model with audio input, a step up from E2B while still laptop-friendly.

models.name: Gemma 4 12B

kv.note: Sliding-window layers are capped at 1,024 tokens. Global layers counted with separate K and V, so this is an upper bound (config sets attention_k_eq_v).

models.summary: Unified multimodal model (text, image, native audio input) that fits comfortably on 12 GB-class GPUs at 4-bit.

models.name: Gemma 4 26B A4B

kv.note: Upper bound; see Gemma 4 12B.

models.summary: MoE model: all 25.2B parameters must be stored, but only about 3.8B are active per token, which usually makes generation fast for its size.
caveats: Storage follows TOTAL parameters; speed follows ACTIVE parameters.

models.name: Gemma 4 31B

kv.note: Upper bound; see Gemma 4 12B.

models.summary: Largest dense Gemma 4 model; a 4-bit build targets 24 GB-class GPUs.

models.name: Qwen3.8 27B
models.arch: dense, hybrid attention (48 Gated DeltaNet + 16 full-attention layers)

kv.note: Only the 16 full-attention layers keep a growing KV cache; the 48 linear-attention layers keep a fixed-size state (not modelled).

models.summary: Native multimodal dense 27B model aimed at coding, professional work and long-horizon agent tasks. Thinking mode is on by default with adjustable reasoning effort.
caveats: The vision projector (mmproj) size shown is a derived estimate from the vision-tower config, not a measured file.
LM Studio's listing states a 16 GB minimum system memory; this is a floor for its smallest build, not a comfortable setup.

models.name: Bonsai 2 27B (Ternary)

kv.note: Assumed identical to the Qwen3.8 27B base architecture.

models.summary: Very compact 27B-class model: the GGUF files are 5.95-7.21 GB. PrismML reports 98.2% aggregate benchmark retention against full-precision Qwen3.8 27B (publisher-reported).
caveats: Runtime restriction: the Bonsai 2 GGUF files need PrismML's llama.cpp fork (CUDA, Metal, Vulkan or CPU). Stock llama.cpp rejects the PTQ1_0/PQ2_0 formats or loads them incorrectly (Hugging Face model card). It is therefore not a drop-in model for stock LM Studio, Ollama, vLLM or SGLang.
MLX builds for Apple devices exist (prism-ml/Ternary-Bonsai-2-27B-mlx-2bit); their file size was not verified in this audit.
Benchmark numbers are PrismML's own aggregates, not independent measurements.

models.name: Bonsai 27B (v1, 1-bit / ternary)

kv.note: Assumed similar to Qwen3.8 27B; unverified for v1.

models.summary: First-generation Bonsai 27B. LM Studio's model page states it runs on LM Studio's stock llama.cpp runtime, with roughly 3.9 GB (1-bit) and 7.2 GB (ternary) footprints.
caveats: Vendor-stated footprints from the LM Studio page; the exact file sizes were not measured in this audit.
Extreme low-bit quantisation can cost quality on some tasks; test on your own workload.

models.name: Qwen3.5 4B

kv.note: Config not read for this size; rough value.

models.summary: Small multimodal Qwen3.5 model for low-memory devices.

models.name: Qwen3.5 9B
models.arch: dense, hybrid attention (24 linear + 8 full-attention layers)

kv.note: Full-attention layers only.

models.summary: Small multimodal generalist with a very long native context and a compact KV cache thanks to hybrid attention.

models.name: Qwen3.5 27B

kv.note: Same parameter count and architecture family as Qwen3.8 27B; assumed identical layer layout.

models.summary: Previous-generation dense 27B in the Qwen3.5 family; Qwen3.8 27B is the newer model at the same size.

models.name: Qwen3.5 35B A3B

kv.note: 10 full-attention layers of 40.

models.summary: Sparse MoE: about 36B parameters stored, about 3B active per token. Storage needs are those of a ~36B model, but generation speed is closer to a ~3B model, and MoE expert offload to system RAM is a common way to run it on smaller GPUs.
caveats: Total parameter count (35.95B) is the Hugging Face safetensors total and includes the vision tower.

models.name: Qwen3-Coder 30B A3B

kv.note: Standard full attention in every layer, so KV cache grows quickly with context.

models.summary: Coding-focused MoE (about 30B stored, about 3B active). Text-only; no vision.
caveats: Active parameters shown as ~3B per LM Studio's listing.

models.name: Qwen3-Coder-Next
models.arch: mixture-of-experts (512 experts, 10 active + 1 shared), hybrid Gated DeltaNet / attention

kv.note: Assumes the documented 12 x (3 DeltaNet + 1 attention) layout with 2 KV heads of 256 dims.

models.summary: 80B total / 3B active MoE built for coding agents and tool calling. The model card recommends lowering the context (e.g. to 32,768) if you hit out-of-memory errors.
caveats: Text-only. Needs roughly 30-50 GB of combined memory even at 2-4 bit, which usually means RAM offload on consumer GPUs.

models.name: Qwen3.8 Flash Next (preview)
models.arch: mixture-of-experts (512 experts, 10 routed + 1 shared), hybrid Gated DeltaNet + Qwen Sparse Attention

kv.note: Architecture differs from Qwen3.5/3.8; KV layout not verified.

models.summary: Experimental preview of the architecture Qwen says will underpin Qwen4. Server-class memory needs: LM Studio lists 96 GB minimum system memory.
caveats: Experimental preview: expect changes and rough edges.
The Hugging Face card recommends dedicated serving engines (SGLang, vLLM, KTransformers) for production.

models.name: gpt-oss-20b

kv.note: Alternating full and 128-token sliding-window attention.

models.summary: OpenAI describes it as running within 16 GB of memory. MXFP4 is the model's native weight format, so there is no higher-quality quant to move up to.
caveats: Text-only.
Configurable reasoning effort; reasoning tokens count against generation time.

models.name: gpt-oss-120b

kv.note: Alternating full and 128-token sliding-window attention.

models.summary: OpenAI states it fits on a single 80 GB GPU (H100 / MI300X class). On consumer hardware it needs about 64 GB+ of combined memory; MoE expert offload to system RAM is the usual approach.
caveats: Text-only.

models.name: Devstral Small 2 (24B)

kv.note: Standard full attention; the KV cache is large at long context.

models.summary: 24B agentic-coding model from Mistral (codebase exploration, multi-file edits, tool use) with image input.
caveats: Context is stated as 256K; the config lists a larger position limit.

models.name: Devstral 2 (123B)
models.summary: 123B dense agentic-coding model (Mistral reports 72.2% on SWE-bench Verified). Server-class: FP8 weights alone are on the order of 125 GB. No GGUF sizes were verified in this audit; a 4-bit build would be roughly 70-75 GB by simple parameters x bits arithmetic (estimate).
caveats: Modified MIT license with usage conditions.
Not offered by the recommender because no measured quant sizes were verified.

models.name: Ministral 3 8B

kv.note: Config not read; typical dense 8B-class value.

models.summary: Compact Mistral model with vision, released as Instruct, Reasoning and Base variants.
caveats: Context limit and KV layout not verified in this audit (rough values).

models.name: Ministral 3 14B

kv.note: Config not read; typical dense 14B-class value.

models.summary: Largest Ministral 3 size; a 4-bit build fits 12 GB GPUs with moderate context.
caveats: Context limit and KV layout not verified in this audit (rough values).

models.name: DeepSeek V4 Flash

kv.note: KV layout not verified; long contexts (up to 1M) may need far more memory.

models.summary: 284B total / 13B active MoE with a 1M-token context. LM Studio lists a single 156.40 GB download and a 156 GB minimum system memory, and also offers it through Bionic cloud.
caveats: Text-only per Hugging Face (pipeline tag text-generation) and LM Studio's capability list (tool use, reasoning). An earlier Atlas snapshot listed vision; that was not supported by these sources.

models.name: DeepSeek V4 Pro
models.summary: 1.6T total / 49B active. Open weights exist on Hugging Face (MIT), but LM Studio offers it as a cloud-only model. There is no consumer-hardware configuration.
caveats: Server/cloud tier only.

models.name: Mistral Small 4
models.summary: Mistral lists minimum infrastructure of 4x H100, 2x H200 or 1x DGX B200, so it is a server-class open-weight model.
caveats: Not offered by the recommender: no verified consumer-hardware builds.

models.name: Llama 4 Scout
models.summary: Meta describes Scout as 17B active with 16 experts and long-context capability; INT4 is targeted at high-end accelerator hardware. Total parameter count and context limit were not re-verified in this audit.
caveats: Open-weight does not mean easy to run.

models.name: Llama 4 Maverick
models.summary: Larger Llama 4 sibling with 128 experts and 17B active parameters. Total size not re-verified in this audit.
caveats: Server-class.

models.name: DeepSeek-R1 (and distills)
models.arch: full model: large MoE; distills: dense 7B-70B
models.summary: DeepSeek released R1 under MIT plus smaller distilled models (LM Studio lists 7B, 8B, 14B, 32B, 70B). The full R1 is server-scale; the distills are the local branch, and are older than the Qwen3.5/3.8 and Gemma 4 generations.
caveats: Legacy reference; no sizes verified in this audit.

models.name: Qwen3 (4B / 8B / 14B / 32B)
models.summary: First-generation Qwen3 dense line with switchable thinking mode. Rough Q4-class sizes from the previous Atlas snapshot (unverified here): 4B ~2-3 GB, 8B ~5 GB, 14B ~8-10 GB, 32B ~19-21 GB. Qwen3.5 and Qwen3.8 are the newer generations.
caveats: Sizes are rough and not verified in this audit.

models.name: Qwen3-VL (2B / 4B / 8B / 30B-A3B / 32B)
models.summary: Vision-language specialists for screenshots, documents and visual reasoning. Qwen3.5 and Qwen3.8 are natively multimodal, so they cover many of the same use cases in one model.
caveats: Sizes not verified in this audit.

models.name: GLM-5.3
models.summary: LM Studio lists GLM-5.3 as a cloud-only model: 753B total / 40B active, coding and agentic focus. GLM-5.3-Flash (320B / 18B active, with vision) is also cloud-only there.
caveats: Cloud reference point, not a local option.

models.name: GPT-5.5
models.summary: OpenAI (23 Apr 2026): designed for coding, research, data analysis, documents, software use and multi-step tool work. Cloud only.
caveats: Reference point for what cloud frontier models offer; not a like-for-like benchmark match for small local models.

models.name: Claude Opus 5
models.summary: Anthropic (24 Jul 2026): positioned for coding, knowledge work and scientific research. Cloud only.

models.name: Grok 4.7
models.summary: SpaceXAI (21 Sep 2026): described as its most powerful model for coding and knowledge work. Cloud only.

models.name: Gemini 3.5 Flash
models.summary: Google's Gemini 3.5 Flash, introduced as the first model of its next generation, combining advanced intelligence with high speed. Cloud only.

harnesses.name: Qwen Code
harnesses.summary: Open-source coding agent that started as a fork of Google's Gemini CLI (v0.8.2) and has since developed independently.

details.interfaces: Terminal UI, headless mode, VS Code / Zed / JetBrains extensions, desktop app (macOS, Windows, Linux), HTTP+SSE daemon, TypeScript/Python/Java SDKs
details.providers: OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Qwen, and any third-party or local model (Ollama / vLLM listed)
details.maturity: Repository showed ~27.3k GitHub stars on the curation date; desktop releases carry 0.0.x version tags, so the desktop app is early.

harnesses.name: OpenCode
harnesses.summary: Open-source terminal-first coding agent with a desktop beta and 75+ providers via the AI SDK and Models.dev.

details.interfaces: CLI/TUI, desktop app (beta), web, VS Code integration
details.providers: 75+ providers; local Ollama, LM Studio and llama.cpp documented via OpenAI-compatible base URLs
details.maturity: Repository (anomalyco/opencode) showed ~211k GitHub stars on the curation date. Built-in build (full access), plan (read-only) and general subagent.

harnesses.name: Goose
harnesses.summary: General-purpose extensible agent, created by Block and now maintained under the Linux Foundation's Agentic AI Foundation; MCP is central to its extension model.

details.interfaces: Desktop app (macOS, Linux, Windows), CLI, API; acts as an Agent Client Protocol server for VS Code, Zed and JetBrains
details.providers: Anthropic, OpenAI, Azure, Bedrock, OpenRouter and local models via Ollama
details.maturity: First released January 2025; governance moved to the Agentic AI Foundation (announced Dec 2025, transfer completed April 2026 per Wikipedia).

harnesses.name: OpenHands
harnesses.summary: Software-development agent platform: browser client (Agent Canvas), Python Software Agent SDK with an agent server, CLI, plus optional cloud and enterprise offerings.

details.interfaces: Agent Canvas web UI (localhost), CLI, SDK/REST/WebSocket agent server, OpenHands Cloud
details.providers: LLM-agnostic; can also drive other agents through the Agent Client Protocol
details.maturity: Repository (renamed from All-Hands-AI to OpenHands/OpenHands) showed ~89.6k GitHub stars. Docker sandbox is optional but recommended.

harnesses.name: Cline
harnesses.summary: IDE-centred coding agent with explicit approval for file edits and terminal commands, plan/act modes and checkpoints.

details.interfaces: VS Code extension, JetBrains plugin, CLI, Kanban board, Node SDK
details.providers: Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini, OpenRouter, Bedrock, Azure/Vertex, any OpenAI-compatible API; Ollama and LM Studio for local models
details.maturity: ~67.6k GitHub stars on the curation date. Every edit and command requires approval unless auto-approve is enabled.

harnesses.name: DeepSeek Harness
harnesses.summary: DeepSeek's agent harness with an everything-is-a-plugin architecture (built on Cordis). Marked developer preview with a warning that compatibility-breaking changes are expected.

details.interfaces: Web UI (default http://127.0.0.1:3080) and the dsh CLI; desktop is referenced in its build targets
details.providers: Not stated in the README content reviewed
details.maturity: Developer preview. The GitHub page showed ~238.7k stars; stars are popularity, not maturity.

harnesses.name: Bionic (LM Studio)
harnesses.summary: LM Studio's agent environment. A session can run on a local model, a cloud model (LM Studio Secure Cloud, zero data retention) or a remote model on another device via LM Link, and supports skills.

details.interfaces: Part of the LM Studio desktop app
details.providers: Local, cloud and remote models chosen per session
details.maturity: Details beyond the model-selection docs were not verified.

concepts.name: Model
concepts.definition: The trained neural network: weights plus architecture (parameters, experts, context length, modalities).
concepts.notThis: Not the app you chat in and not the software that runs it.

concepts.name: Runtime
concepts.definition: Software that loads model weights and executes them on your hardware: quantised formats, GPU/CPU split, KV cache, an API endpoint.
concepts.examples: llama.cpp, LM Studio, Ollama, vLLM, SGLang, MLX
concepts.notThis: A runtime does not decide what to do; it only produces tokens.

concepts.name: Harness
concepts.definition: The layer that wraps a model in an agent loop: prompts, tool registry, permissions, context management, planning, sub-agents.
concepts.examples: Qwen Code, OpenCode, Goose, OpenHands, Cline, DeepSeek Harness
concepts.notThis: Not a model and not a runtime. It connects to a runtime or a cloud API.

concepts.name: Agent
concepts.definition: The running system that acts: model + runtime + harness + tools working together on a task.
concepts.examples: Qwen Code driving Qwen3-Coder-Next served by llama.cpp
concepts.notThis: An agent is a behaviour of the whole stack, not a single downloadable file.

concepts.name: MCP
concepts.definition: Model Context Protocol: an open protocol for exposing tools, resources and prompts from servers to AI applications (clients).
concepts.examples: A filesystem MCP server, a database MCP server
concepts.notThis: Not a model, not a runtime, and not a security guarantee: review what each server can access.

concepts.name: Skills
concepts.definition: Reusable instructions, scripts and workflows an agent can load on demand for a specific kind of task.
concepts.examples: A code-review skill, a release-notes skill
concepts.notThis: Different from MCP tools (which are callable capabilities) and from memory (which is state).

concepts.name: Memory
concepts.definition: Information an application persists across sessions and feeds back into context: notes, preferences, project facts.
concepts.examples: A project notes file loaded at session start
concepts.notThis: Not the model's weights, not the context window, and not the KV cache.

concepts.name: RAG
concepts.definition: Retrieval-Augmented Generation: fetch relevant passages from an external index at question time and put them into the prompt.
concepts.examples: Search your PDFs, then answer using the retrieved chunks
concepts.notThis: Retrieval supplies context; it does not change the model or replace memory.
